utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. Mr. Karadzic, I take it that you have a team member to introduce to us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Excellency, thank you. This is Mr. Aleksandar Vucic, my legal adviser, my associate, because Mr. Robinson will be absent for a few days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Welcome, Mr. Vucic. There's a brief matter to deal with before we begin today's business. The Chamber has been informed that the Defence and the Prosecution agreed that the document marked for identification as MFI D342, and the document admitted as Exhibit D354, should both be reclassified as public documents. The Chamber, therefore, instructs the Registry to reclassify these two documents as public. Mr. Karadzic, let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Minister, let us just establish a bit of a link. Yesterday, we dealt with 30088, that's the 65 ter number, but now let's call up 31839. That's the 65 ter number we want now. Mr. Zepinic and I are conducting a conversation, and we are discussing the implementation of the inter-party agreement. We are saying that we're worried because behind our back, Serb cadres are being manipulated, and he said that someone had made some proposal, and so on and so forth. So could you now please have a look at the next conversation. I'm talking to Mr. Simovic, the deputy prime minister on the very next day. He's the deputy prime minister, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He's not a member of the SDS either?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He was an official of some sort in the previous system as well; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And he was expelled because of some mass arrests in Ilidza. Do you remember when 250 Serbs were arrested in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and now he is the president of the Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ha-ha. He complained about something and then he was removed from State Security; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now please have a look at page 1. See where it says "Sorry"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I got a document here that I should sign for some Kezunovic." Simovic: "All right." Karadzic: "Do you know what this is all about?" Simovic: "Well, you see --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simovic: "You see, I suggest perhaps maybe they had certain consultations at the MUP. We urgently need to resolve the issue of assistant minister for people's defence in the domain of communications. We fear that, considering the way they do things, they might impose someone. They will not impose a minister ..." "Yes."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the next page in Serbian. The first three, and then we're going to move on a bit lower.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The minister of traffic and communications is from HDZ." "Yes." "The assistant for communications in the MUP is from the SDA:" Karadzic: "Excuse me, for a moment, Mr. Simovic. Just a minute." There is a break, and then, "Hello," and then move on to where Karadzic says: "Vito, yes, Vito."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Interpreter's note: next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Karadzic: "No. Vito just lied to me ; right?" Karadzic: "Devedlaka proposed Suka, and then the Romanija people. That is not correct. It wasn't the Romanija people nor Devedlaka. He was the worst man in Romanija, Suka; right?" Karadzic: "Yes." "For such a significant Serb position there. So what does he want to do now. Profanity. Does he want to sell out Serbian positions? I now caught him in this situation, that things are not the way he says they are. Profanity. He is not entitled to privately appoint anyone. He should call a Serbian board of experts and say, 'People, we have a particular Serbian position. Who will be appointed to that position?' I'm not running Serb politics off the top of my head. I call the elders here, the Academy of Sciences, and I ask and check my ideas."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the next page in Serbian. In English, this was page 3, probably. Yes. So now could we have the next page in Serbian and the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Well, Simovic is saying. Miodrag Simovic here: "Fine. Here, I will let Vito sport [as interpreted] propose, the one we agreed would start functioning as of this morning. This is the first day and it is not functioning well. Let them take it, let them agree among themselves and make a proposal to you. The one they decide, propose ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, on the basis of this, is it not clear that the party is not insisting on making appointments, it is the Serb collegium that is supposed to make appointments, so any kind of manipulation on the part of the SDA is avoided?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, so far in my testimony I've been saying that personnel in the police were not appointed by the party, but by the personnel people. First, it was Vito Zepinic, and after that I took upon myself these personnel affairs for the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you imagine how many times we would be talking if the inter-party agreement had been honoured?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Tieger had two or three intercepts, conversations between you and me. My mother called me at least five times to give jobs to some people who were poor, who were from the neighbourhood, whom we knew, et cetera, so there were no pressures from the party. We appointed personnel on the basis of our own conscience and their qualifications. There were some interventions coming from local level, either addressed to me, or to you, or to Vito Zepinic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And towards the bottom of this page, well, yes, do you agree that this has to do with some person called Kezunovic, who was a good professional and who they want to move from the police to the Ministry of Defence, and that we are suspicious; we think that they are doing that because they don't want any Serbs to be in the Communications Department?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Kezunovic personally. He worked in the police force, in the Communications Department, for many, many years. It was the SDA that got the number-one post in communications, and this man was the number-two person in that particular department.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the system of communications that was used in order to wire-tap our conversations illegally?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The State Security had a separate system, and this is a different one from the Public Security, from the MUP headquarters. Munir Alibabic, with his associates, was the one who was illegally wire-tapping our conversations from the Sarajevo Centre.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is this page 5 in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please read this, at the bottom of this page, in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan Karadzic: "Yes, a complete man, an expert, capable, and they moved him. It is all I guarantee to you, that I am horrified with what Vito is doing to us. Now, listen to me. It should not be done like that, privately ... give positions of one's own accord. I asked 50 people for Simovic."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "They said Simovic was excellent. Simovic would be deputy prime minister. You are not my cousin, nor did I have any private interest in appointing you. On the contrary, I saw for myself what kind of person you were." Simovic: "Fine, dear president. Here, let me inform you about this too. I am glad, and I am glad that are you not upset, and there is no need that they upset you in a totally inappropriate way."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Further down, page 6 in English, and Karadzic is saying: "Well, they're not here as a private affair."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Karadzic: "They're not here as a private affair. Serbian people are sharing government with Croats and Muslims here. They were charged with being in that government on behalf of the Serbian people. No one can be in that government for their private interest."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the next page in Serbian, and in English it's page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I said if you could refer to that portion of what Simovic was saying.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simovic: "Gentlemen, ministers, I was very tolerant for two months. The prosecution and my commission -- I listened to Jure --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sorry, who is Jure?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jure Pelivan was the then prime minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A Croat; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, an ethnic Croat, yes: "It was discussed for two months. No more giving way. I said, if necessary, we would block the work of the personnel board and do everything in order to sort this out properly, just to let you know."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you read on?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Karadzic: "We will help them get what is theirs, and that's it."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, thank you. You know, to a considerable extent, how it was that I worked. The indictment portrays me as a very stern and authoritarian person who was in charge, when I asked that democratically-reached decisions be implemented. You're a man who belonged to the administration. When democratic decisions are supposed to be carried out, are they supposed to be carried out properly? Should any impropriety be allowed, and should they be carried out lackadaisically?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, you always asked that the agreed concept of government and state administration be fully implemented. You do react sometimes. Sometimes you can be a bit rash, but there were no pressures exerted to do anything that was not in line with the inter-party agreement or based on law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Put a pause, please. Now you can put your question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it not undeniable, Minister, that in 1990 I was not a candidate for any particular position in government or Parliament?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first heard of you in 1991, in the beginning of 1991. You were not in a single organ of government in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it not undeniable that I did my job at the clinic all the way up until the first barricades were set up in March 1991?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went to your clinic at the School of Medicine, and that's where you had your office.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we mark it for identification? Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that this has been already marked for identification as D281. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D181, could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, I am trying to stick to a particular chronology to see how we are getting closer to the war from the elections period so that the participants, primarily the Trial Chamber, could see how political life developed in Bosnia, and where it went, and who was to be blamed for that. This is a document dated the 28th of August. Let me remind you. Do you agree that July and August were characterised by the activities of Filipovic, Zulfikarpasic, myself, Koljevic and Krajisnik, that is to say, the MBO and the SDS, in order to create a historic agreement between the Muslims and the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zulfikarpasic, head of the MBO Party, represented the Muslim people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you read the first paragraph here? Do you agree that by then, there was a great deal of tension already? The war was on in Croatia, right, and the tensions had already spilled over into Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, especially in the parts of the Krajina close to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were rumours rife already then, very dangerous rumours, and it wasn't only rumours; there was already a process of illegal arming and military organisation that was underway?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the war gradually spilled over --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Mandic. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is a duplicate of a 65 ter 14837, which does have a translation, and that may be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. 14837.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, this has been admitted as Exhibit D264.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we also see the English translation, just to jog our memories.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the war was already going on in Croatia. It had already spilled over to the peripheral areas of Bosnia and Herzegovina. At that time, do we have quite a lot of refugees from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to read the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I advise you herewith that I have reached an agreement with Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, president of the Party of Democratic Action, and Mr. Stjepan Kljujic, president of the Croatian Democratic Union, that these three political parties establish observer groups tasked with monitoring all developments in their respective communities that affect or may contribute to a deterioration of inter-ethnic relations and cause conflict."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last sentence, please read the last sentence also.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At the same time, in the co-ordination with the representatives of the Party of Democratic Action, and the Croatian Democratic Union in your municipality or region, you are to advise the president of the Municipal Assembly and the Public Security Station chief in your municipality of the full composition of the observer group."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the last sentence of the second paragraph, do they say that they should indicate any differences of opinions in the parties regarding the said developments; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this a measure calculated to objectivise the rumours and to place under political control the developments in the field, always in compliance with the state organs, the municipality president, and the chief of the Public Security Station? Do you agree that that was a measure that could have led to the preservation of peace?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers be so kind as not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you're advised again by the interpreters not to overlap, so please bear that in mind, that since you are speaking the same language, you should put a pause for the interpreters to interpret what you're saying. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll do our best. I forget myself. Can we see D266, which has already been admitted. And now, from August, we are moving on to September to see what the SDA is doing at that same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you remember, Minister, in August the SDA sent a letter to the effect that the Yugoslav People's Army was not allowed to inspect the mobilisation cards. Do you agree that basically mobilisation had been carried out through branches of the Ministry of Defence in the municipalities, but overall the entire system of defence had been subjected to the Federal Secretariat of National Defence, i.e., the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Later, we shall see that Mr. Izetbegovic, himself, admitted that we had violated slightly, as he put it, some laws. Do you see this document, and were you aware of this document at the time of its issuance?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please read the first three paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Party of Democratic Action, notice of full readiness of communications and monitoring by the SDA. "Since the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina is increasing in complexity by the hour, we have decided to declare full readiness of communications and monitoring of all activities in the territory under the control of the SDA. "Hence, enclosed will you find a form which will give us information enabling us to give instructions and co-ordinate activities in the future. "Under point 1, monitoring movements, a monitoring service is to be organised throughout the entire municipality (inhabited by Muslims) and all information is to be sent to a central desk in the municipality, accessible 24 hours, from where information is to be forwarded every two hours by telephone to the Sarajevo SDA switchboard." And the telephone number is given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please read also the next one.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Under point 2, observation of features, information is to be provided every 24 hours and as needed," something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "As necessary"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, "as necessary."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see page 3 of this document. Probably in the English it is page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are these now the points elaborated? Can we see page 3 in English also? Has the monitoring of movements of military convoys, of tanks, of APCs, of railway traffic, military convoys, extraordinary trains, air traffic, the observation of facilities of BRX [phoen], the security of BRX, the strength of BRX, combat readiness, security, military installations, locations, the activities of all these. Can you summarise in order for me not to read it all out, what was to be monitored?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Practically everything. Everything that moved on the ground was to be monitored.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this an eminently illegal activity against one's own army, or what precisely -- was any state organ entitled -- did any state organ, not to mention party organ, let alone party organ, have the right to undertake such monitoring?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is evidently unlawful. It is a mono-party exercise. It is unconstitutional, it is illegal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is an admitted document. I just wanted us to remind ourselves of what the Party of Democratic Action was doing in September. Although we did say that together -- but not these activities, but the three parties should monitor jointly the activities of this kind and take action, here the SDA is assuming upon itself the monitoring of these activities following placing under surveillance its own army, its own units, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see 65 ter 30216.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is my telephone conversation with the late President Milosevic. I'm not sure of the date, but I'm sure it is somewhere in the text. Possibly, this has been offered also by the OTP. But, at any rate, it is the 9th of September, 1991. The indictment actually likes this episode very much, whereby it is to demonstrate how I co-operated with the army, with organs of Serbia and Yugoslavia, to save Milan Martic. Here, where he says: "Manista nijotisa" [phoen], can you start from that point? It is, for instance, the 10th row -- line from the top, when Karadzic says --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Karadzic: "Yes." Milosevic: "We need more substantial forces so that -- to resolve this situation. It is night-time, and helicoptering can be used, but we'll see how to take care of this at dawn. Jovica just told me a helicopter has been sent to pick this guy up." "Nothing has been sent. That is the problem. I'm afraid that the MUP, this Muslim part of the MUP, will turn him over to the Croatian MUP, and that would mean war in BH. No one could stop it then."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The two next ones, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "No one could stop it then?" Radovan: "No one would be able to stop it then, but I'm not sure if war suits Alija, because he wants to ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Can we see the next page. In English, it is also page 2, the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Until that is done, do you remember the crisis around the illegal arrest of Milan Martic in Otoka, near Krupa, on the Unani [phoen] Bosanska Krupa, namely, of Martic and a number of JNA officers, on the night of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here we have shown and, if necessary, we can again see this intercept, where I was called by Malko Koroman from Romanija at 2 a.m. and he said that all of Romanija was unsettled because of the arrest that the they had heard about, so people were actually anxious because -- do you think that that was because this was an unlawful arrest, that of Martic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can remember, Mr. President, I and Avdo Hebib went out in the field and dealt with that problem then, but there were tensions on account of the arrest of a couple of officers. And Milan Martic, who was at the time in the Bosnian-Herzegovinian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now finish with this sentence, where it says: "Here ...," at the top?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan: "No, we are going to use this for political purposes here today our meeting with Izetbegovic. Again, they are simply going for a division of BH, and we are going to implement a regionalisation and introduce our MUP wherever we are in power, because what they have done is inadmissible. We won't believe these people gather spontaneously. The SDA has both the power and influence there. However, if they -- if the military does not send a helicopter or an APC there as soon as possible to get the man out, then that will be a great danger because this Milan guy is in constant contact with the BH MUP, the part that we do not --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Control"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, "control."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then go on, please, where I say: "This is impossible." It is also page 2. Radovan says -- that's the last third --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "But this is -- but this is -- I mean, it is unbelievable that we do not at all know who of the BH MUP is in contact with the Ustashas and Tudjman. Also, chaos in BH certainly suits Tudjman because he wants to internationalise the conflict, and maybe this is true of Alija too."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page in Serbian, actually, the two following pages. And in English, it is page number 4. Instead of "conflict," it should be said "chaos."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, towards the bottom of the page, Radovan: "Let them do this as soon as possible. We'll have a catastrophe on our hands. That will be the spill-over -- the expansion of conflicts in BH, and people from Romanija have informed me that they were preparing to block Sarajevo. No one will be able to get out of Sarajevo. It will be a disaster. I'm going to call Izetbegovic now to tell him this. I'll talk to you later, then." "Okay."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At an Assembly session, if you recall, I spoke about how peace was in our hands and chaos was not in our hands, but we were in the hands of chaos. Can you contemplate that anyone would have been able to control developments had they actually turned over Martic to the Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they wouldn't have been able to control developments.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we mark it for identification, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, marked for identification, yes, just like all other intercepts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI D365.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 30236.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And until we see that document: Minister, this is my conversation with Mrs. Plavsic. I don't know who called whom, but that doesn't really matter. Towards the end, the English page 2 and the Serbian 1, towards the bottom, Biljana says: "Davam kasim" [phoen]. Can you go from there?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Biljana: "Let me tell you, Radovan, I'm very worried about the situation at the SUP." Radovan: "Ah, what's the matter now?" Biljana: "Well, I heard they -- they sacked Nedjo Vlaski, I mean they scrapped his job, you know." Radovan: "No, they can't, we can."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify. Is SUP and MUP one and the same thing?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Biljana, as the president of the council for the protection of the constitutional order, was this her field of activity, state security?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By virtue of her office, she was the superior of the entire MUP and she controlled the legality of the work of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now see the next page in Serbian? In English, it is page number 3. Can you see this passage where Biljana says: "Now I want it from him in writing"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Biljana: "Now I'm asking him to submit the report to me in writing, but I would not wait for it because the situation is really clear there. You should talk to Alija and say that." Radovan: "We'll probably have it today." Bijeljina: "We will." Radovan: "Today we'll probably have these talks with them, and I'll say no talks until ..." Bijeljina: "That's right." Radovan: "Until they appoint, at the SUP ..." Biljana: "Until they stop deciding which Serb will work where."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this all happening nine months after the formation of the joint coalition government?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you go on from the words: "Correct, correct"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan: "Until they stop deciding ..." Biljana: "We will separate a part of our SUP that's it. We'll also carry out a cantonisation of the SUP. You should know we'll do that." Radovan: "We will do all that, we will do all that." Biljana: "They should be told that in so many words. Let me tell you, we have to be very energetic now and tread very energetically, and this is the first and the right place, and they are playing games with us."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that they were removing Serbs from strategic positions? They had nothing personal against Major Vlaski; what mattered was that there should be no Serbs in that service?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Politicians were deciding all this, and the people were just wait to go see what was going to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the politicians were responsible and accountable for their people for their regularity of political activity?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, being marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D366, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 18231, please. 18231.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We're still in the month of September. This is a dispatch from the chief of the Security Services Centre, Banja Luka, to the Public Security Station, Prijedor. Do you see the date, 19 September 1991, and the document? Please look at it, and you can even read the first passage.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the chief of the CSB is writing this dispatch to inform the chief of the Public Security Station in Prijedor that five persons of Muslim ethnicity should be assigned to the SJB Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says, actually: "I have been informed by MUP dispatch number ... that the following persons have been assigned to the Prijedor SJB."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And here we have the names of five policemen. It's not a long document. Can you read it, please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of it, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This Ilijas Aliskovic, concerning this passage where it begins with: "Other workers ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "With regard to the other workers, for whom I have not provided a recommendation for employment to the MUP of the SR BH and for whom security vetting has not been completed, who are not covered by the current number of police staffing specification posts in Prijedor SJB, and whom I have not even informed I received reports that they have begun to work at your Public Security Station despite the fact that they are not covered by the number of police staffing specification posts. I hereby ask you to inform me with whom it had been agreed that the number of posts in accordance with the Prijedor SJB staffing specification was exceeded, and the reason why. "I do not approve of these workers continuing to work in your Public Security Station, and I have informed the republic minister accordingly. I hereby ask that in all future cases, you consult me when proposing candidates for employment, because personnel policy is the business of the chief of the centre."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do I understand this correctly, that in this case, unlawfully and bypassing the usual procedures and vetting procedures, people were employed with the Prijedor Public Security Station without the knowledge of the chief and unlawfully?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I read this dispatch, Mr. President, the chief of the centre is basically protesting with the chief of the Prijedor SJB because the centre is their superior, and yet they had been circumvented in hiring. That is contrary to the laws of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and he demands that this practice stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There are three points here. It was done without the knowledge of the chief of the centre, and bypassing the procedure, plus the number of posts was exceeded?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's all stated in the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that consistent with your knowledge about the illegal action of the SDA in restructuring the MUP in favour of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, that September they began with creating a Muslim army within the Ministry of the Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the decision to establish the Patriotic League was made on the 31st of March that year?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was made in 1991, but I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that they still recognise wartime service to their members as of the 30th of April, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And from what I know, the Muslims had the largest army in Europe. They had more members of the Patriotic League and veterans than active personnel in NATO forces. They had 20 -- 200.000 registered members, and the federal budget cannot support it. They are in huge problems.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D367, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D1893, please. I hope it has a translation. This is a record, minutes from the session of the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, 21st September 1991. This is not the right document. 1D1893.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The minister of the interior was present, Mr. Delimustafic, and I believe you know about this meeting. Could you please look at the document? Izetbegovic, Blaskic, Kljujic, Boric, and Ganic all attended. And as guests, Doko, Delimustafic, and others. They also invited non-members to attend?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was customary when they had specific topics on the agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read the agenda?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Report of Presidency members Biljana Plavsic, Ejub Ganic, and Franjo Boric, on the talks in the General Staff of the SFRY armed forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the next passage, we see that on 20th September, 1991, and in accordance with the conclusions of the Presidency of 19 September 1991 -- can we now see the next page in Serbian -- these three members of the Presidency went to the General Staff of the JNA for talks. It says -- and I apologise to the interpreters. In English, we need the next page.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 1: "Municipal assemblies may, if the situation so requires, and with the consent of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, carry out a partial mobilisation of regional units of the Territorial Defence in their territory. Military authorities will be asked to issue the required equipment and weapons to these units."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read paragraph 3, where it says Biljana Plavsic did not agree with paragraphs 1 and 2? Do you agree that if the Serbian members disagree, and Koljevic seems to have not been present, this disagreement has the force of veto in such serious matters?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The principle in accordance with which the Presidency worked, especially in matters crucial to the republic, was consensus. Decision-making with agreement of all the members of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this paragraph 2, does it now become clear that Serbian young men in the JNA were under the command of JNA officers, as recruits, as conscripts, whereas the Territorial Defence was at the disposal of presidents of municipal assemblies? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that according to the Law on National Defence and Social Self-Protection, just like the president of the Presidency was president of the Council for National Defence, in the same way every municipal president was the president of the Municipal Council for Defence?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And every municipal president was thereby at the head of the local Territorial Defence unit, of course, under the superior command of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be admitted now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D368, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D01403, please. While we're waiting: This is again dated 21 September 1991. It's a document from me, from the Serbian Democratic Party, instructions to all municipal boards of the Serbian Democratic Party. I hope it has a translation. No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please read this for the record as a translation?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Instructions to all municipal boards of the SDA --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's not long, but it still may be helpful to note this is a duplicate of 00956, which does have a translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I thank the Prosecution. Can we have that translation displayed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please continue?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The wartime forces of the police are currently being mobilised. There are rumours that up to 100 per cent of the forces are being mobilised, although the bodies at the republic level can mobilise only 50 per cent of the forces. There are also rumours that only Muslims are being called up, or that Serbs do not respond to the call-up, which would result in the creation of a Muslim police force and would create conditions for a civil war. "Please follow closely the developments in this respect. "The instruction is that Serbs are to report to the reserve police force. "Keep us informed."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was I rather modest -- was it an understatement when I said this was a rumour and guess-work?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, rumours are -- is information about events that are not necessarily true. But you must have had information and reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this, indeed, a dangerous -- a flammable situation, because could the Serbs have been concerned because the potential enemy for these people could only have been Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this consistent with what they decided that they -- in the Presidency, with which Biljana Plavsic disagreed?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were these reports basically true? To what extent were they true?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MUP would have had such reports, and they were, for the most part, true.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D369, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D1894, please. Could we zoom in? I don't know if we have a translation. I believe we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll tell you about the signature. It's the minister of the interior, Alija Delimustafic, 26 September 1991. Could you read the first half of the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pursuant to an order of the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, reserve forces of the police have been activated, and accordingly police work is being carried out under special circumstances. "Pursuant to Article 63 of the Law on Internal Affairs, members of the police force are considered as authorised officials while engaged in performing the duties of public and state security. Under the said provision, reserve police officers have the same rights, obligations and responsibilities as active-duty police officers. However, it has been noted that reserve police officers do not always act in accordance with the law, the rules of performing public security duties and the mandatory instruction, on the rules of conduct and internal relations among authorised official personnel of the organs of the interior."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that all this was happening over a certain time, does this also following from the activities of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, against which the Serbian side voted?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was supposed to be decided by consensus. Biljana did not agree with that decision.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D370, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D1909, could we have that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it, Minister, may I ask you or may I remind you that we had not taken the Ministry of the Interior. I'm referring to the Serb people of Bosnia-Herzegovina that were represented at the time by the SDS, but they could have been represented by another party too; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The one-third of power had to be in the hands of the Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the coalition agreement that you had signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But also on the basis of the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that was good practice as well, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since we were not given -- or, rather, we didn't really ask for it, the minister of the interior, that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Tieger, you have another number for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The translation for this document should be with 18243.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Let's pull it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, let me ask you, Mr. Minister: Since we were not given the top positions, and they sabotaged the appointment of our people to the number-two and number-three posts, does this document show that the link between these two ministries of force proved to be very dangerous? Let me relieve you for a while and let me read the first paragraph. The Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the Presidency and all the members and so on, and then the text. I mean, it even goes to the General Staff and the Federal Secretariat. That's the Federal Ministry of Defence in Yugoslavia. And it says here: "The Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at its session held on the 23rd of September, 1991, adopted a conclusion allowing the Ministry of the Interior to engage upon issues issued by the minister, additional police reservists from the contingent of undeployed military conscripts registered with municipal secretariats for national defence." Does this mean that the ministry -- or, rather, that the Presidency is taking over military conscripts and turning them into potential policemen?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, that was the creation of a Muslim army in the territory of the former Yugoslavia or, rather, Bosnia-Herzegovina through the Ministry of Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this connection, the Ministry of Defence sent a dispatch -- there is a mistake in the translation. They'll probably change this during the course of the night, but the witness said that that was the beginning of the creation of a Muslim army in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, through the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: That is exactly what we said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Isn't that right, through this joint organ a mono-ethnic army was being created of one people?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Not through the military police, but through the Ministry of the Civilian Police?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said through the Ministry of the Police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the interpreters confirmed what you said. But, Mr. Mandic, can you take a look at the last page of this document? Are you a member of -- were you a member of the Presidency, Mr. Mandic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why did you sign this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please see the first page again? Because, Your Honours, the Ministry of Police, where I was assistant minister, was being manned unlawfully. I was in charge of the legality and legitimacy of the work of that ministry. There were certain conditions under which the reserve police force could be called up; that is, imminent threat of war, major natural disasters, and everything else that would disrupt normal life in a country.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be of assistance? Perhaps confusion is being created here because it says the Presidency, the government, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, am I right that as assistant minister, you are sending this to the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina? This is not a document to the Presidency. This is a document of the ministry that is being sent to these addressees?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then there is a misunderstanding, then I did not understand His Honour's question properly, because I sent this document to all the state organs that were in charge, pointing out that this was illegal, that the reserve police force was being called up in an irregular way. I did not understand this. The question that was put to me was why I was sending this document, although I was not a member of the Presidency myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now it's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this connection, the Ministry of National Defence submitted to the municipal secretariats for national defence an instructive dispatch. That's the republican ministry of Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: An instructive dispatch ordering them to compile lists of all registered, undeployed military conscripts and forward them to the responsible Public Security Station, and so on and so forth. May I remind you or may I ask you, Mr. Minister: Do you recall that throughout that year in particular, ever since the war broke out in Croatia, the Muslim leadership practically prohibited military conscripts from responding to JNA call-up?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. May I just explain this document a bit? All military conscripts are being called up here, and that is not in accordance with the law; that is to say, all military-aged men who had done their military service between ages 20 and 50, they were supposed to report to the closest police station to be issued with weapons and uniforms and be placed at the disposal of the police. There was nothing extraordinary going on. There wasn't an earthquake, a flood, or anything else that would jeopardise the normal life of a particular republic, this one. So there was no legal grounds for calling these people up. In this letter, I make all state organs aware of this; not only in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but also in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to go back to this particular term used here, "undeployed." Since the Muslim and Croat leaderships in Bosnia-Herzegovina practically forbade the members of these ethnic communities or peoples to respond to JNA call-up, and since the Serb side had to respond to a greater extent because the JNA was being unmanned, who would then be these undisposed military conscripts that the Presidency is speaking of? Who would they be, in terms of ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's explain this a bit, Mr. President. There was a war going on in the Republic of Croatia between the Croatian people and the Serb people. Intentionally or unintentionally - in my view, intentionally - this war was being transferred to other parts of Yugoslavia, especially Bosnia-Herzegovina that was a multi-ethnic state. A certain climate was being created that reflected what was happening in Croatia, and it was based on a lack of confidence in one's own army in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Of course, that was being carried out by the Muslim side and the Croat side. The Croats, of course, were linked to Zagreb, and they were supporting their compatriots in the war against the Serbs in Croatia. And the Muslims saw their chance to create their own state independent of the Serbs and Croats. We are going to see all of that later, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Although you confirmed that yesterday as well, does this show that the undisposed conscripts are Muslims and Croats, whereas the Serbs are in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, not to complicate matters further.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And these undeployed Muslim and Croat military conscripts are now unlawfully being called up into the police that is not run by the JNA but by the Muslim-Croat coalition in part of the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Mr. Tieger was putting questions to me about 1991 and the beginning of 1992, we saw that one of the bosses in the Serb police, in his letter, pointed out that military deserters who were ethnic Croats and Muslims were being admitted into the police, and that was a problem that was hindering the work of the police more and more, having culminated at a certain point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to read a certain part from the one-but-last page. You say here: "Because of the aforementioned, we ask the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina to re-examine their request for an additional increase in the reserve police force, or, rather, to see whether it is necessary to increase the reserve police force in relation to the number that was established in the decision of --" Perhaps the next page in Serbian now and the last page in English: " ... decision of the Government of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1988, and to explicitly forbid the manning of the reserve police force by certain individuals that haven't been cleared beforehand, and that such persons should be disarmed and demobilised from the reserve police force." Was this your attempt to have things become regular and lawful once again?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to explain that a few moments ago when His Honour put his question. These were unlawful decisions of state organs that were not in charge of that particular matter. That is to say, apart from the personnel levels envisaged by law, police stations were being manned in an unlawful manner. People were being given uniforms and weapons en masse. These were people from other republics. Also, these were people who had deserted from the active-duty army. That was the problem that the police was facing in its work. They had no security clearance, they were simply unknown. There were persons from Serbia, from the district of Raska, there were persons from Croatia, there were persons who had lived abroad in various European states, Arab states, and very often we came across persons who barely spoke Serbo-Croat, the then official language, who did not know -- or, rather, who could not find their way in Bosnian towns because they simply were not familiar with the area. That created fear and a lack of confidence within the Ministry of Police, itself. It culminated when Mirsad Srebrenkovic came instead of Hilmo Selimovic. I would like to inform the Trial Chamber of the following: Hilmo Selimovic was assistant minister for personnel affairs. He was a member of the Muslim people, an eminent person from Sarajevo. He was replaced overnight, dismissed for no reason whatsoever. There was no due process applied, and Srebrenkovic, who was a citizen of Croatia, was appointed. He was working at the Mesihat of the Grand Mosque in Zagreb in Croatia. He was a hodja by training. That was his educational background. He had a degree in Theology from the University of Cairo. Can you imagine how astonished we were when a hodja from a mosque came to be appointed assistant minister for personnel affairs? At this moment, Your Honours, I can say that he went back again to the Mesihat of the Grand Mosque in Zagreb. I mentioned that in the Stanisic trial. We long-standing policemen, who were basically atheist, we grew up in a socialist society, we did not really pay much attention to religious affairs and religious services, we go to a colleague's office who had replaced yet another Muslim in the very same position, and there he was praying. Can you imagine how astonished I was and how confused I was? At that moment -- from that moment onwards from September or, rather, October, hundreds of people came to certain police stations in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Overnight, people were being admitted, the kind of persons I spoke of a moment ago. For instance, in the center of Sarajevo, in the municipality of Stari Grad, the Old Town, which normally has about 80 employees, in the beginning of 1992 or, rather, at the end of 1991 there were 600 persons who were admitted to the reserve police force of Stari Grad, under the leadership of Dahic [phoen], Ismet, on the basis of decisions made by this hodja who works at that mosque in Zagreb to this day. I really do not think this requires any further comment. That is my personal view. Your Honours, we had good co-operation with colleagues who were ethnic Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mandic. I thank you for your kind and detailed explanation, but please bear also in mind that Mr. Karadzic has only a limited time, so please be brief. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, let's continue -- it's time -- I note the time. We'll have a break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Could this document be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D371, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, Mr. Minister: These people, these foreigners, criminals, et cetera, who couldn't speak good Serbo-Croat, who were admitted to the MUP in contravention of regular procedure, did they have all the powers that a regular policeman has; an ID, uniform, armaments, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were admitted to the reserve police force according to the Law on the Interior. They had all the powers, as stated by Mr. Alija Delimustafic, as all other policemen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D2047.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And while we wait, I'm going to ask you this: This is a conversation between you and me on the 26th of September. We seem to be having some difficulty leaving September behind us. It was a very intensive month, in terms of developments. There were quite a few developments. Let me ask you this: Am I right when I say over a year prior to the outbreak of the war, there was a crisis in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe the name of the person Musanovic stands out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the monument to Ivo Andric, the sole literary Nobel laureate that we ever had, was raised to the ground?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. And, by the way, he was a Croat by nationality, but his monument was torn down in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that he was a Catholic, but a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Sorry. He was a Catholic, but he introduced himself as a Serb.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go down a bit? Do we have translation for this now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So we are talking on the 26th of September. I'm asking you, "What are you doing?" You say: "I'm having a meeting." And I say: "Okay, you have your people. It seems that things have started up there in Visegrad. There are criminal complaints -- there is an avalanche of criminal complaints. Come, put your act together, a status being introduced." You say: "Yes, yes." And then I say: "No, this is not in the Serbian land, so I can see that Zupljanin has sent a very fair report from Krajina where the Serbs are doing stupid thing." He said, "So there is no --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we go to 30284, we'll have a translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, this is MFI D207.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is the one already used by you, Mr. Karadzic, and tendered.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it seems so. But as this is a direct conversation between me and Mr. Mandic, can we see the second page now, please, in the Serbian. It is evident that I am commending the fact that Zupljanin is also referring to Serbian folly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And on the second page, what do you say?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mandic: "President, we have to establish the rule of law. We can't do otherwise. I have talked to these people from Visegrad, these people of mine."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Karadzic: "Yes." Mandic: "And I agree with them that all criminal complaints, et cetera, Rato Runjevac [phoen] and his deputies think Nozica came to see me today." For the benefit of the Trial Chamber, Rato Runjevac was the prosecutor, chief prosecutor in Sarajevo, and Senka Nozica was his deputy, and now she's actually a Defence counsel here at The Hague. Karadzic: "Uh-huh." Mandic: "So we have agreed with the prosecutors to elevate this to a higher prosecutorial level for this person to be extracted from Visegrad and for legal proceedings to be instituted against him. This cannot remain the way it is because this will cause blood among the people there. There will be a conflict between the Muslims and the Serbs, and then what will happen?"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, and slow down for the benefit of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I should like to draw your attention to here where I say "Jeste, Alija Izetbegovic." But before that, I should like to clarify this: Izetbegovic and I received people from Visegrad, Serbs and Muslims, in order to diffuse -- ease the situation, and this is what I said about it. You can read it. Alija Izetbegovic says --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the translation. Radovan: "Yes. Alija Izetbegovic is saying -- he's asking that Fikret of his --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page in English, too, please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, "Fikret," he says, "if the Serbs run down into Sjemce, into town to take revenge and to kill Muslims, will they pick out good Muslims from the bad? No, they won't," he says, "they will take one after another. Well, then do not let an idiot estrange you from the Serbs, because then the Serbs will come and will not select who to beat, but will come across someone who is innocent." Mandic: "Well, Mr. President, here I am, working all day on this, and Visegrad and Mostar and the information about the war and everything else."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, you also say you want to be an artisan, a craftsman, an objective person, and to follow the regulations; nothing else?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan Karadzic: "I'm telling you now ..." Momcilo Mandic: "I want to be a craftsman, an objective person, and to abide by regulations, nothing else." Karadzic: "It will only be good when this -- we will have to, however, this unfortunate Simovic is also working 15 or 16 hours. You have to work hard until the situation is sorted out." Mandic: "That is no problem at all."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now refresh our memories a bit. Do you recall that some extremists in Visegrad terrorised Serbs, stopped pilgrims going to Ostrog [phoen] monasteries, pulled out the beard of a priest, tore down the monument to Ivo Andric, and set up barricades intercepting the JNA column and sending it back to Serbia, not allowing it to pass, although it was the regular army of that country?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, that was a long time ago. I know that there were incidents, that a group of Muslim lads tore down the monument of the Nobel laureate monument of Ivo Andric. I know there were excesses based on nationalist feelings, and we, together with the Sarajevo region, tried to identify the perpetrators to have them prosecuted, to have the Prosecutor Rato Tunjevac [phoen] with his associates undertake the necessary measures and institute the regular criminal proceedings. I cannot remember every detail, in fact.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As this has been admitted for identification, there is no need to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure I have a trace of this intercept having been tendered before. D207 seems to be the different one. I have to check with the Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it has not, then I will move that it be so admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, can you confirm the accuracy of this conversation you had with Mr. Karadzic at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think this has been tendered before. Yes. This 65 ter 30284 has never been tendered, so, as such, we'll admit it, because as one of the interlocutors, Mr. Mandic confirmed the accuracy of the conversation. But on a related note, Mr. Karadzic, you've tendered many intercepts in which you were one of the interlocutors. If you agree with their accuracy, we can admit them without having to mark them for identification, can't we? One may argue that by adducing them, you are actually adopting them, and also, furthermore, one may argue that they are helpful to your case. What do you think about this observation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, in my introductory remarks I said that we were being wire-tapped unlawfully, but this is a source of extensive information and it shows how much effort we invested in order for things to be regular. The principle -- the contention/objection of the Defence is that they have had no right to do so, but I have not yet come across an intercept that I would consider forged. These that we have offered are authentic, and I remember these problems and these talks. Perhaps we can leave this for later to reconsider, but I do think that you will be admitting them, or that is why I am tending them, just in case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, we'll come to a more comprehensive analysis to this issue -- we'll come to this issue in a more comprehensive way, but do you like to make any observation on this issue, since I raised it, albeit briefly?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The same observations that occurred to us, Your Honour, and with respect to those -- yes, to both the intercepts that have been tendered to date and the general reflection on the intercepts to be tendered in future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it there are several categories of intercepts you will tender -- you have tendered or you will tender in the future in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understand the Defence position about the legality. I think that's been addressed. I think once we have crossed that Rubicon, the intercepts should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come to that issue later on. But, in any event, this intercept has been admitted, in light of the -- Mr. Mandic's confirmation. So we'll give the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D372, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My principle objection is that they did not have the right to do that, but the Defence reserves the right -- if we should come across a document that can be considered to have been edited by Munir Alibabic, then we reserve the right to either ask for a recording, an audio-recording, or to be given the opportunity to check it. Can we see 1D2023.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But can I confirm, Mr. Karadzic, before you move on, there has been no such documents so far that have been tendered or used? That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not noticed that anything has been doctored or forged so far. I have not followed it very closely, but I have not noticed any distorted or doctored recordings so far. But that needs to be checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do not have a Serbian version here, unless the OTP has one. So it is 1D20 -- and so on. This is from the 4th of November, Mr. Minister, and it is also one of your documents. And you say -- I'm going to read it in English: [In English] "Simultaneously, with a significant increase of the total number of crimes in our republic in the recent months, an increase was recorded in the number of crimes which, given the targets, implementation methods, extreme brazeness and aggression of the perpetrators, in their entirety represent increased social threat with various dire consequences." Can we see page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On pages 2 and 3, and this is your report to the all chiefs, and you enumerate on page 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Here's a hard-copy version of the B/C/S, if that's needed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, if you can carry on with the English translation, I will let the witness take a look in B/C/S, without having to put it on the ELMO. That may be speedier, but I leave it to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be fine. I'm reading in English: [In English] "Below is an outline of only a few examples of such successful operative work done recently. Identification of the perpetrators of aggravated vulgarity committed at the petrol pump in Ripac, near Bihac, when the petrol pump workers were killed. Identification of the mother of a young man, attacked and killed while he was together with his girlfriend in a parked car at the [indiscernible], very short near Tuzla. The zoning of the double --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We do not have the right page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]: [In English] " ... near Bratunac and the identification of its perpetrators. The solving of a multiple crime of violent behaviour, causing public danger, et cetera, in Visegrad, and the taking of legal action against its group of perpetrators." [Interpretation] You see all the things you enumerate; the murder of a JNA officer, a JNA reservists in Banja Luka, and so on and so forth. That's page 3 in English. The entire document is available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see that in this interim report, you also mentioned this example from Visegrad to illustrate the massive incidents of crime? Does this fall within your regular duties?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have, and we will still remain in September, 1D1892. Can the previous document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is Mr. Mandic's document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the last page? Well, that's a document written and signed by Mr. Mandic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D373, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If Mr. Usher could deliver that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I briefly interpret this document? At the top, we see that on the 9th of September, through the Ministry of Information of Bosnia-Herzegovina - look at this document - Serbian senior employees of the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina put out a public communique about their discontent, and the irregularities, and cases of unlawful behaviour that have been noticed. Legal provisions are being violated, those that govern the conduct of security services, such as bypassing the deputy minister, the scrapping of the post of the deputy under-secretary for state security, inconsistent and irregular personnel policy wherein Serbian employees are replaced by obedient Serbs, which is particularly grave in the Security Service, the hiring of a large number of persons who have criminal records and who are currently under criminal proceedings, issuing of orders without the knowledge of the minister or his deputy, the creation of an anti-army atmosphere as reflected in the written order of the MUP, for the police to be involved in taking over the military records from the JNA, and issuing official IDs to people who are not employed by the MUP. Is this an authentic communique, press release, made by Serbs in the senior posts of the joint police force?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. While I was at the head of this collegium, we made this public, all these illegal actions and irregularities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: You resorted to this move after writing to the Presidency, the minister, the Defence Ministry of Yugoslavia, et cetera. You resorted to making public all the information about irregularities and unlawful conduct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you follow the press? Do you know that two Sharia policemen were caught these days in Sarajevo unlawfully photographing certain installations and facilities?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read about this terrorist act in Bugojno involving the murder of some policemen. I didn't read about what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll bring a document showing what the president of the Ministerial Council of Bosnia-Herzegovina stated about this, and this is how far things went -- have gone since 1991. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
