utterances.text: Unless it is objected to, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D374, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D01362, please. I believe we've seen this document before. This an audio-recording of the session of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the prime minister with the highest-ranking personnel of the Defence Secretariat of Yugoslavia and the General Staff of the JNA, including Kadijevic and all the other personalities. On page 5 -- can we see a passage on page 5. I will try to summarise this. There was one person here, Mr. Donia, who said that the presence of the JNA in Bosnia-Herzegovina resulted in rising tensions. However, here Alija Izetbegovic says that they will try hard to avoid any problems that the army had in Croatia and that the situation in Bosnia included the presence of a large number of illegally-armed people. Now, can we see page 42. This one is marked "35." We need page 42. This is page 42. This is what Mrs. Plavsic says. She complains about big problems, and she says: "You have heard about some of these problems, but I believe we have to go to the very sources, and don't be afraid that I'll be talking for a long time when I say, 'Go back to the source.' The source of everything is that the highest state organs in Bosnia and Herzegovina are circumventing, to put it mildly, federal provisions, especially federal provisions concerning the JNA." And this is a very good reading, these minutes. We need the next page, 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that the Federal Secretariat of Defence and the General Staff attended this meeting in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know they came for a visit. I don't know exactly when, but it was in the autumn of 1991, Mr. President, to be briefed at the Ministry of Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here: "Concerning the Crisis Staff," Mrs. Plavsic talking. This is the 15th of October, after the enactment of the illegal decision on independence. They receive General Kadijevic and his associates from the General Staff. And she says: "As far as the Crisis Staff is concerned, on which I used to be," it was formed by the Presidency, "as far as the Crisis Staff is concerned, the one on which I used to be at the beginning and that had been created by the Presidency, with the idea that the Crisis Staff should deal with the problem of refugees that we have in this republic, and trying to create a more or less normal life for them, and providing for the good functioning of roads, the Crisis Staff," and I believe also General Vukosavljevic realised this, "the Crisis Staff of the Presidency assumed also certain powers that rightfully belonged to the Council for National Defence. And when I realised that the Crisis Staff was discussing these problems, I resigned from it. The Crisis Staff should really deal with the problems that are outside of the field of work of a federal institution called the JNA." Now we need page 44. Question to you, Minister. Were you aware that Mrs. Plavsic had resigned from the Crisis Staff because she objected to its conduct? It was a crisis staff originally created by the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe she also froze her membership in the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 44, this is Mr. Izetbegovic talking. He's not best pleased, but Mrs. Plavsic said what she said, and he says: "We are fully aware that by proclaiming the independence and neutrality of BH, we maybe violated some laws, but there are laws and laws. We are also aware that there are certain things that could be violations of federal legislation." Was the Presidency able to see, from your writings, that these laws were being breached?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the dispatch that has been admitted, yes, I did state everything very clearly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we need not quote any more from this document. This is from the Council of National Security. It may have been tendered before, but I don't know if it has been admitted or marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You refer to this document as Presidency sessions?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I am not sure what the status of this document is, but I remember, having heard once from Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, that she would check into the matter of whether the Prosecution has it in the house, and also afterwards Ms. Edgerton reported there was none. When this was put to Mr. Donia, he raised the question why he should be shown this excerpt, while there should be a more authentic document, but I don't think the Prosecution has the entire Presidency minutes or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's an accurate recollection and recounting of the information available about this document thus far and the discussions that took place about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So shall we mark this for identification, pending translation, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And in addition, we will -- I mean, once translated, of course, we want to look at the extent to which it appears to be intact, excerpted, and that -- the source of the extraction of whatever excerpts might exist. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Give me a minute. So shall we -- with that caveat, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D375, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I don't think these are excerpts. It's the entire transcript of that meeting, which was extremely important, because the Supreme Command of the Armed Forces and the Defence Ministry came to that meeting with the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But we are at your disposal for any check you wish to run. It's a very well-known meeting. 1D41, please. We'll deal with it very briefly. This is 10 days before that meeting. Mrs. Plavsic addressed the public by speaking to this newspaper, "Politika," of the 4th of October. She repeated everything she had said to Izetbegovic. She says: "Imagine this situation." "Imagine -- can you imagine this situation? The National Defence Council is not functioning. The Crisis Staff has taken it all over." And a bit below, she says that: "It was left to a basically informal group to deal with major problems. The SDA believed that the Crisis Staff had been created in order to bypass the Serbian representatives, Mrs. Plavsic and Mr. Koljevic, in major decision-making."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that correct? Do you agree with this judgement by the Serbian members of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted? Just for the record, the title is "The BH Crisis Staff Meddling in Other People's Affairs": "Dr. Biljana Plavsic does not wish to participate in the work of the Crisis Staff of Bosnia-Herzegovina," and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D376, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 65 ter 30341, please. It is quite possible that it has already been admitted into evidence as a P document. Am I right? Has this been tendered already by the OTP? No? All right. So we have identified it. It is our conversation -- it's a conversation between you and me on the 13th of October, two days before that well-known Assembly session when the Muslims and Croats passed the declaration on sovereignty. Can we have a look at the second page, please, both in Serbian and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, let me ask you, Mr. Mandic: As a lawyer, do you agree that the Constitution can be amended only as envisaged in the Constitution, itself, in a constitutional manner?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in all our Constitutions, in order to amend the Constitution, a two-thirds majority was required, at a minimum, in the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what the Constitution says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I please ask you to read this: "No, no, that is, I mean ..." That part.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan: "No, no, well -- I mean, there is chaos. Besides, he's trying something there now, but he will not tell me that they are preparing a transfer for Draskovic, and we had agreed previously that there would be no chance of a transfer of any Serb without the consent of ..." Momo: "Mr. President, that is not all right. Cedo Kljajic will go to the Police Department, and he will be replaced by that person for public, for this ... that's okay, President." Karadzic, Radovan: "Wait. That cannot be done without our agreement and our consent. That is unacceptable as a method, and tomorrow members of Parliament will ask me for answers concerning this situation. This is intolerable, simply intolerable, to have any personnel changes take place without our knowledge and our consent, because that is a mechanism which they used to manipulate us, and Serb members of Parliament are fed up with all these attempts to proclaim independence. Alija Izetbegovic admitted to us ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Momo says: "I heard." And I go on: "... that this sovereignty means independence." Do you agree that this is nine and a half months -- almost 10 months from the time when the coalition government was established? Nevertheless, there was no implementation of the electoral results and the inter-party agreement, and it has to do with important, sensitive positions in the police that they are illegally being -- that they are illegally turning into a party army?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D377, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D2026, please, could we have that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is one of your documents again, Mr. Minister, 1D2026. Does the OTP have this in Serbian? Well, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Almost, by definition, in light of the nature of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. It has an ERN number. In the meantime, let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be lowered a bit so that we identify a translation mistake? No, no, actually, we'd like to have the beginning of the page. We'd like to have a look at the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, do you agree that "SR BH," on the 28th of December, does not mean the Serbian Republic, but rather the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, mistranslation, Your Honour. Socialist Republic, not Serbian Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just so we know. It's a tiny mistake, but it may be important. You are sending this to all security service centres, public security stations, and the Sarajevo MUP. It has a position that is a bit different; right? So you say that --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise. May I have the B/C/S? Can I have a copy from Mr. Tieger so that I can follow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's coming. You're hearing the printer working.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Let me just have a look, and I'm going to return it intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at it. I'm going to read it out in the English language: [In English] "Number 02/0-12248 of 19th of December, 1992 [sic], and dispatch number 08/4-2687 of 27th of December, 1991. "In our dispatches numbered and dated as above, we informed you that the minister of the interior had issued an order prohibiting MUP managerial or supervisory officers from signing formal decisions pertaining to employment issued [sic] (admission, posting, retirement, and so on), and ordered the reconsideration of all formal decisions issued in this sphere since September the 1st, 1991, and at the same time halted all payments based on these decisions. The minister of the interior also ordered that all measures be taken to call to account any officers who violated this order." [Interpretation] A bit further down: [In English] "Any action aimed at implementing these decisions constitutes a criminal offence." [Interpretation] Page 2 now: [In English] "... constitutes a criminal offence." [Interpretation] In the beginning, it says: [In English] "... and Assistant Minister Mirsad Srebrenkovic are taking measures contrary to the order of the minister and are also instigating others to commit unlawful acts." [Interpretation] And now some articles were violated: [In English] "The deputy minister shall render decisions on the rights, duties, and responsibilities of employees of O -- Ministry of the Interior. Accordingly, the minister and the legal rights -- has the legal rights to render decisions on employment rights, including by means of an order, which in this case shall have the force of a regulation and not an administrative enactment, and which shall be applicable generally for all employees in the MUP." [Interpretation] Can you tell us, what compelled you to send this? This was sent on what occasion?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Mr. Mirsad Srebrenkovic was appointed instead of Hilmo Selimovic as minister of personal affairs - that is what I talked about before the break, that this was a religious teacher from the Zagreb mosque - the man created chaos in personnel affairs in the police. At meetings of the professional collegium attended by the minister, we said what was going on. And when Mr. Delimustafic, the minister, realised that the man had made hundreds and even thousands of decisions that were unlawful concerning individuals that I already spoken of, not to repeat myself, he issued an order to annul all of those decisions that were illegal or unlawful. The assistant minister spoke against his own compatriot. He said that the minister's order is wrong and that he was right in the first place, and that all these persons who are unlawfully employed could remain within the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that this Mr. Srebrenkovic derogated the minister's order; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely, that's what I was trying to explain, that he opposed the dispatch sent by the minister, and he said that the minister was not right. He said that he was right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And thousands of these unlawfully-admitted policemen stayed on with their weapons, IDs, and powers?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interpretation of it is that in the leadership of the SDA, it was this right-wing fundamentalist wing that prevailed, and they annulled the decision of the minister, who was an ethnic Muslim and who realised how terribly unlawful the personnel policy in the police force was. He publicly opposed his superior officer, and all of us present here know what subordination means in the Ministry of Police, where the number-one man is an institution, per se, with a wide spectrum of powers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D378, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that the Translation Service is going to change this mistranslation of the document. 1D2895, could we have that document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I return this to Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D1895, that is another document of yours dated the 9th of January, 1992. It is sent to the Federal Secretariat of National Defence. We can't see it yet. It's also sent to the General Staff and to General Veselinovic, the head of the Military Secret Service or, rather, the Military Intelligence Service, then the Federal Secretariat of the Interior, to the president of the Presidency of Bosnia, Mr. Izetbegovic. Yes, we can all see it. I don't have to read it out. We can see all the addressees here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You call this document "Obavijest," "Notification." Could you please read the first paragraph? Could I please ask you to read the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. "Subject: Notification. "Recently, on several occasions, I have pointed to the overtly partisan conduct of the former assistant for the police and now adviser to the minister of the interior, Mr. Avdo Hebib, whose conduct causes ethnic -- inter-ethnic hatred and distrust throughout the republic, thereby threatening peace in the republic."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have to read all of it. Could we have the next page in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you to tell us a bit more about what it was that compelled you to send this notification, which is rather alarming and dramatic, to all of these addressees?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Avdo Hebib, when the multi-ethnic or multi-party MUP was being established, he was -- he held the post of assistant minister. That was very important. It concerned 10.000 policemen in uniform. There was a change, and he became an adviser. However, he started operating in a partisan fashion in the police, and he started arming the reserve police force, and, against the law and against the staffing system, he started handing out weapons without the knowledge of the police and without the knowledge of persons who were in charge of that particular matter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the next page in English so that the participants can follow all of this. The transcript does not reflect that at first he was assistant minister for the police; that is to say, that he was the main person as far as the police was concerned. After the minister, he was the first person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Avdo Hebib is a psychologist by training. In the socialist system, he worked in the infirmary of the Republican Ministry of the Interior. The authorities expelled him then, because when he tested Serb candidates, he did not give them positive evaluation. He eliminated them in that way, and he prevented them from joining the police force. At one point in time, Dusko Zgonjanin, the Republican chief of police suspended him and expelled him. When Veljko Kadijevic resigned as commander-in-chief of the Army of Yugoslavia, and when Blagoje Adzic replaced him, he called up the entire reserve police force in Bosnia-Herzegovina, particularly in Sarajevo, although he was just an adviser then. He did that along political party lines. I know what the reason was for him to do that, but I believe that it is not relevant to these proceedings. If you suggest, I may tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That number, those thousands of military conscripts, undeployed military conscripts that the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina were unlawfully transferring to the police, that is to say, they were stealing them away from the JNA and transferring them to the police, were they supposed to be re-subordinated to Avdo Hebib?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Avdo Hebib was creating a parallel armed force in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From the police and from the reservists that were being re-subordinated to the police?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the reservists also, the police in general, and everybody that had served their military service, those who were reservists in the army and were of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I move to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D379, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 5842. While we wait, let me tell you we shall see on the cover page this is the "Official Gazette" of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, number 1, issued on the 15th of January, 1992, and it contains decisions. On the first page, it is the decision of the establishment of the Assembly of the Serbian People, as well as the first documents that the Assembly of the Serbian People adopted. Can we now have 324007324. That is the ERN number. That is the penultimate page -- actually, two pages from the end of the Serbian version. Please scroll up in the Serbian version so that we can see the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I know that you did not deal in politics much, but do you remember that at the political level, parallel with what was happening criminally in the state organs, primarily in the MUP, do you recall that on the political plane the Serbian side demanded that the illegal decisions be rescinded, and after a couple of days it made its own moves, establishing the Assembly first and subsequently the Republika Srpska, et cetera? Do you see that this is a decision on the establishment of the Ministerial Council of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: At what page should we look to in English; 23?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not have it in English. Ministerial Council, but the previous one in English. No, in fact, it is okay. Actually, can we see the next page -- or, rather, let's have this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see, Mr. Minister, that this is a decision -- a published decision on the establishment and election of the Ministerial Council of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and can you see that Dr. Miodrag Simovic was elected its president and that the members listed here are, in fact, representatives of the Serbian people in the joint government?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that all of these actions of ours had been provoked by the unlawful behaviour of the Croat-Muslim coalition and that we always gave them some 10 or 15 days to re-institute legality and constitutionality?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please rephrase your question? I'm not quite clear on what you are asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 14th and the 15th, we had a Joint Assembly session. We vetoed the adoption of the memorandum or declaration of independence, but they disregarded our veto. We walked out, and they took that decision. We asked, publicly and officially, for them to annul that decision, and then on the 24th of October we established the Assembly of the Serbian People; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, Mr. President, at that time there were frequently instances of out-voting by the majority of the MPs in the Joint Assembly as well as by members of the Cabinet in the government. So after this, the decision was taken to establish a Serbian assembly and to form a ministerial council comprising personnel from the joint government that had been functioning in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that that was a direct response to the violation of our constitutional rights?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see -- or, rather, do you agree with me that the Serbs, both MPs and Cabinet members, continued to work in joint organs and that this was a preparation -- or, rather, a response to the unlawfulness that obtained, and that the Ministerial Council comprised people who were in the Cabinet anyway?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the decision to set up the Assembly of the Serbian People, it is stated that all the MPs will remain working in the Joint Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 3 in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see, in the bottom left corner: "Decision on the status of officials, leadership, workers, officials, and other officials in republican state organs, where it is confirmed that they will remain in --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. So that we can follow as well in English, probably page 6 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Excellency, that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it is stated there that these organs -- or, rather, these people who form these organs shall continue to work normally, and these organs shall remain as a correctional agent of the unlawfulness that obtained?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision -- about a decision of the Assembly of the Serbian people that all the MPs should remain working in the Joint Assembly, all the government members in the joint government, and other officials in the other joint bodies of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That was an Assembly decision, and this is the decision.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 32400 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. Could the speaker please repeat the number. That was too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, could you repeat the number again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ERN number in the Serbian 0044-7324. And if I can be of assistance, it says: "Decision on the establishment and election of the Ministerial Council of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina." On the top, it says "page 10," if that is of any help, "page 10," in the Serbian variant. That is 4. We need page 10. Where it says "page 4" in the heading, it should be page 10 in the Serbian version. Thank you, that's it. Now, if you can find the appropriate page, the corresponding page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that inter alia, Mr. Vito Zepinic also accepted to be the minister of the interior in the Ministerial Council? That will be the next column in this page. You can see it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 24 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that Vitomir Zepinic was the first Serbian minister for the police.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it has been admitted as Exhibit D296.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It has been admitted. Can we now see -- we are already into 1992, Mr. Minister. I'm not asking you many questions about the political subjects and developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that the Assembly sessions of the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina were transmitted live on Bosnian-Herzegovinian TV?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that was customary at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 65 ter 00377.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in Zenica -- I saw this in "Oslobodjenje" the end of February. Slobodanka Hrvacanin was protesting because a Serb had never been appointed to his proper place which rightly belonged to him in the MUP. So this was some 14 or 15 months after the setting up of the government. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, we have a letter by the Serbian Democratic Party. It has a number, it bears a date. It says here -- or, rather, can you read this first part?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Personnel Matters"? That: "1. All decisions on the employment of about 1.400 people in the MUP of the SR BH who are not within the staffing scheme plan are to be annulled." Secondly: "All managers, managerial and other staff who do not meet the requirements of the Law on Government and the Rules on Internal Structure and Staffing Scheme in the MUP or the SR BH are to be relieved of their duties (i.e., those who do not have appropriate degrees, who have a criminal record, et cetera. ) "3. A citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina of Muslim nationality is to be appointed deputy minister of the interior for personnel. During his appointment, the legal procedure is to be respected, consent of the governing parties."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this item adopted because this Srebrenkovic was a Muslim but not a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not a national of Bosnia-Herzegovina, a citizen. He was a citizen of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you read on until point 4?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Personnel of Serbian ethnicity are to be appointed to posts that belong to them (chiefs of public security in Zenica, Livno, and Mostar, commanders in Visegrad, Bratunac, Srebrenica, Stari Grad, Bosanski Petrovac, and Breza, chief of traffic police in Jajce, et cetera.)"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that 14 months after the establishment of the joint government, the Serbs did not get any influential offices and a fair share in the police in the majority of the Bosnian municipalities in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For instance, in the Stari Grad municipality, which is at the very heart of Sarajevo, the republican capital, there was never a commander of the police force appointed of Serbian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Once we had occasion to see here that there were a couple of these municipalities, for instance, the number of Serbs in Sokolac would be managed by a like number of Muslims in Pale, and we had this system you should employ a like number of our people or we shall have your people dismissed?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My personal experience was a clash with Malko Koroman from the Pale municipality, also a municipality in the city, because these people in Pale would not appoint a Muslim as commander of the police, because in the adjacent -- the adjacent Stari Grad municipality wouldn't do so for or with a Serb. It was an eye for an eye, quid pro quo, and in fact I and Malko Koroman had a falling-out because I asked him -- Malko Koroman, and I ordered him, actually, that he should not be looking to others who were acting in contravention of the law and in contravention of the inter-party agreement, but that he should take proper action, nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it is out of doubt that this -- out of doubt that this is associated with a reciprocal treatment in the adjacent Stari Grad municipality?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I tried to point out to him that he should not look to the other municipality to see what they are doing, but that he, himself, had to abide by the law. But I couldn't persuade Mr. Koroman that that was a proper course of action.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the next page, please, in both languages. "Organisational Matters." Can we see the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out these two paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Organisational matters." "1. The Security Services Centre to be set up in Trebinje urgently. "2. The State Security Sector of the CSB in Sarajevo is to be brought up to strength, and the legality of the operation of this sector is to be examined, especially the illegal use of the methods of equipment of this service against officials of Serb ethnicity (secret surveillance, wire-tapping, photographing and search of apartments and official premises). In view of this, we demand that Munir Alibabic, Sarajevo State Security Sector head, be removed from office for putting this service at the disposal of the SDA."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next one?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roman numeral III: "I hereby authorise and order Mr. Momcilo Mandic, assistant in the MUP of BH, to participate in solving personnel and organisational matters in the MUP of BH on behalf of the Serbian Democratic Party."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now see page 1? Do you agree, Minister, that on the 1st and 2nd of March, barricades were put up, and we'll be discussing it in your examination, you gave a series of interviews, one of which deserves our attention?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This letter is dated 6 February. It's the culmination of rifts and disagreements in the Ministry of Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, read the passage before "Personnel Matters." I wrote this on the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of February: "Pursuant to the conclusions adopted by the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina of the 2nd of March, 1992, relating to the necessary personnel and organisational changes in the MUP, we demand:"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the proper date is 6 March, not 6 February?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This must be a typo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that on the 2nd of February, Mr. Dukic attended this session of the Presidency, where his demands were accepted; namely, to disband the Crisis Staff, to implement the inter-party agreements, and that happened on the 2nd of March? 1st March, barricades; 2nd March, barricades torn down, and Dukic attended this session of the Presidency which accepted the demands of the Serbian Democratic Party to correct -- to redress the irregularities that led to the erection of barricades?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, the immediate reason for putting up the barricades was the killing of that member of the Serbian wedding party in Bascarsija, and that happened on the 29th of February. I remember that well because it was a leap year. You were travelling somewhere in Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you call Belgrade Europe, then I was.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's to the best of my recollection, whereas Rajko Dukic had taken over -- in fact, the staff, headed by Muhamed Cengic, deputy prime minister, negotiated, of course, with great assistance from the Serbian members of the Ministry of Police, trying to preserve safety and prevent incidents when armed masses take to the streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it was on the basis of these conclusions of that session of the Presidency that I sent out this letter, asking that qualified people, including you and others who were not SDS members, asking that the inter-party agreement be implemented and that all irregularities in the joint MUP be stopped?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was one of -- a series of efforts to ensure legality in the work of the police. And I believe that the Presidency, headed by Mr. Izetbegovic, had embraced all these positions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted before the break, with the proviso that the actual date is the 6th of March, because it refers to events from the 2nd of March?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. This will be admitted. But it just disappeared from the transcript. What was the date on which Mr. Dukic attended this session of Presidency? Line 5 of the previous page, you asked about on 2nd of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was on the 2nd of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The exhibit number will be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit D380.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for half --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may add, that will be a separate point. This is a very important meeting, and I will lead evidence about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Has this document been admitted? I think it has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now ask for 65 ter 30593. I believe the Prosecution also has the translation. Yes, we have a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Minister, you see this is the 10th of February. I'm talking to Mr. Zepinic, Dr. Zepinic, as my secretary calls him. Can you read the words: "Aha, Vito," please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Aha, Vito, please. With us, we are suffering the consequences now in Bratunac of not having appointed a Serb as militia commander, over there they are establishing the border-line facing Serbia and setting barricades up."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page in English -- in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Read this part where they talk about a barrier, setting up a barrier, somewhere in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Karadzic speaking: "They're creating barriers, not letting Serbs from Serbia come in. They don't let anyone get out. That bridge is in the Serbian part of the centre. I'll call now." Karadzic says: "It's in the Serbian part of down-town. We are insisting, anyway, that Bratunac be --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not find this passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that beginning with Ottoman times, there was always a Serbian neighbourhood down-town and a Muslim neighbourhood down-town, and they were like two separate areas?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the Serbian one was called Taslihan, and there was a cafe called Europa?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I learned that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where the church was and the brewery that was called Latinluk?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the Turkish area of down-town was called Bascarsija, which is a Turkish name?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in Brco, to this day there is a Serbian down-town, and when the Ottoman Turks invaded, that remained intact, whereas the other neighbourhoods were given different names?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were under Ottoman rule for 500 years, and that area was mostly inhabited by Serbs. The centers of various places were divided into Serbian and Turkish areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The municipality called Centar, has this Serbian neighbourhood, all the way up to Kosevo, the Old Town --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Stari Grad also has this old town inhabited by Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in Sarajevo, generally speaking, Muslims -- or, rather, Turks, before them, were tradesmen, and they held the center of populated areas, whereas the Serbs were on the periphery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mean the Serbs that did not convert to Islam, because the Muslims are mostly Serbs who converted to Islam; you know that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I learnt about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now let us explain to the Trial Chamber what we really meant when we referred to Serbian municipalities. Do you remember that because of all these problems in the functioning of the political system, we proposed, and the proposal was accepted by the other two sides in the negotiations, and agreements had been reached, in all places where it was not possible to do otherwise, the municipalities would be divided into Serbian areas; the Serbian center and the Serbian villages in the municipality would be a Serbian municipality, whereas the Muslim centers and the Muslim villages would be the Muslim municipality?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was that during the Lisbon Agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Lisbon Conference was still ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that at that time, it was not a condition or a requirement to ensure territorial continuity?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it was envisaged that in all places where one community had a number of 20.000 or 30.000, the members, they were allowed to create their own canton or their own municipality?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say positively, but I know negotiations were going on at the Lisbon Conference, and that was dealt with in the Lisbon Agreement, but I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this concept of dividing an existing municipality into two or three different municipalities is familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that it was suggested.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this document MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just in case, Mr. Mandic, do you recognise -- no, you haven't heard this tape. Very well. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D381, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's necessary to identify the voice of Mr. Zepinic, we can do that. But since this is only to be MFI'd, we can do that later. Now, 65 ter 05413. I believe that was tendered by the Prosecution, it has been admitted. Is it right that this is a P exhibit now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P1083.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, this is already 11 February 1992, 14 months -- rather, 16 months after the elections, and 14 months after the creation of the first joint democratic government in Bosnia-Herzegovina. And instead of getting solved, problems only multiplied; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this meeting, in fact, the result of these multiplying problems that had come to completely paralyse the state machinery and legal conduct in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was this meeting held?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Banja Luka, at the Bosna Hotel, at the hotel's restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it was not a secret location?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were served by waiters of all ethnicities. You know that Bosnia was multi-ethnic at the time, as it is today, and there were no secrets. And as I confirmed in the Stanisic/Zupljanin case, when asked by Ms. Korner, the minister of the police was notified of this meeting and these minutes, among other people, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since you discussed part of this document with Mr. Tieger, I'd like to draw your attention to something Mr. Stanisic said. The passage begins with "the SR BH MUP."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The SR BH MUP is being divided by the Muslims, not the Serbs, contrary to what the public is being told. Since the SDA Party, for example, there are 1.000 men in the Stari Grad police reserve, of whom only about 30 are Serbs, and these barely have uniforms, in contrast to the others who are armed with the most modern weapons."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page in Serbian, and let the English page remain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Minister, who convened this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Apart from Mr. Zepinic, who nobody had any confidence in anymore, was this meeting attended by all the senior Serbs in the police?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All Serbs, both in the Public Security and in the State Security Sector, although truth to tell, not all the Serbs who were supposed to be appointed to the State Security Sector had been appointed. There were few Serbs in the State Security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say they were not appointed because of that sabotage against the appointment of Serbs to the positions due to them?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were any of these people members of the Serbian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, none of those present was a member of the SDS, and they were mainly people with long years of service on the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mean to say they worked in the police even under the previous system, but they were so loyal that they continued in the police in the Serbian republic later?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were career policemen, people who graduated majoring in humanities or had degrees in law and who were dedicated to their jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I meant to ask: Did they work also under the one-party system before?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But nobody could say that they were ideological zealots; they were men of their own trade, professionals?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that was the basis for keeping them on the police force, because the SDS wanted all services to remain professional, rather than transforming them into party-run services?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the Law on State Administration prevailing in 1992, people employed in state administration and the judiciary were not politically active and did not have any party affiliation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you come to convene this meeting? Whose idea was it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can summarise all the evidence I gave today about these problems that cropped up. It was mainly calls from police chiefs on local level. They experienced a lot of problems, and they called for an effort to solve them, to deal with them. And that's how this meeting was organised. I invited all the experienced staff from the lines -- ranks of Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mean to say that you were exploring every possibility to restore legal and lawful and regular conduct in the joint police, and all these efforts had come to not before you convened this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's obvious, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You discussed this with Mr. Tieger, but I just want to say that at the bottom of the page, Cedo Kljajic says that Senad Rekic and Avdo Hebib are circumventing him and going on field missions without his knowledge, et cetera. Next page, please. Kljajic says: "We Serbs are the only ones who are operating lawfully, as opposed to the HDZ and the SDA. How else would it be possible to buy several thousand Motorolas without any one of them having been stored in the MUP depot? I categorically state that the SDA and the SDS cannot work in the same MUP, and if Nenad Radovic's proposal is not implemented within seven days, I will resign." And so forth and so on. Andrija Bjelosevic says one of the police stations in the Doboj CSB has not had a commander since August. Andrija Bjelosevic also says: "Since a truck with the weapons for the SDA has been seized in retaliation for that, the MUP had not been sending us weapons at all, but only sending weapons to police stations where Muslims live. We have also received complaints against Deputy Minister Vitomir Zepinic who signs decisions on the informant of Muslims in Doboj but will not sign for Serbs." I do apologise to the interpreters, but I hope they have this on the screen, the document, that's why I'm rushing this way. Could I have the next page, please. Can you read what Stanko Stojanovic says? "DB Gorazde"; right? He never had any contact with the Serb Democratic Party. Can you read what he says?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanko Stojanovic: "It is my opinion that we are late, in terms of organisation. Gorazde talks to Hebib and Pusin every day, and they get instructions. The SDA has its check-points where they seize goods. Their warehouses are full, and they are announcing that they will blow up the bridges on the Drina River. They are also activating extremist groups which will first attack the Serbian population. Their attack will surprise us unless we organise the Serbian MUP as soon as possible."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is one of the most moderate members of State Security? Ideologically, he is totally uncommitted. He is a pure professional, not any kind of Serb extremist, and do you agree that this assessment of his is a dramatic one?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move on to the conclusions, page 6 in Serbian. It's probably 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, Minister, although we are negotiating with Cutileiro at the time, we had not been given approval to establish our own MUP. That was the 22nd of February. Is the a Serbian collegium of the MUP being established here or a Serb MUP? That is point number 1.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Serbian collegium is being established here attached to the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was adopted here were 19 conclusions that are supposed to help attain constitutionality and legality in the work of the police in the republic. Also, this is signed. Did you show this to Minister Delimustafic or did someone else familiarise him with it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, with regard to this meeting, there was a public invitation, as it were. Of course, I contacted my colleagues every day, ethnic Croats and Muslims. We talked about these problems. I invited Mr. Delimustafic to attend this meeting in Banja Luka, where problems were represented from the local level by Serb officials in certain regions of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Of course, Delimustafic was either busy or did not want to come. I cannot recall now. When we returned, I reported to him about the meeting and the conclusions, and we agreed to do our very best to prevent a break-up in the MUP. Rather, we should decide what should be done at policy-making level, what the Lisbon Agreement would amount to and negotiations in Sarajevo, and that, therefore, we should behave on the basis of decisions made by policy-makers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a document that was admitted as a P document. Minister, if we look at these 19 conclusions, is there anything that is unjustified or illegal?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there is no such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did anyone challenge this from the point of view of constitutionality and legality?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people were not interested in this, especially not Assistant Minister Srebrenkovic. They had their own mission, and they were out to accomplish it. So I think that this was a plea that no one responded to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 10724 now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this has been admitted as Exhibit P1112.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, is this your telegram that pertains to this meeting? Could you read it out to us or could you tell us what the essence is?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this meeting, I returned on the 12th to Sarajevo, probably. I had a meeting with Minister Delimustafic on the 13th. I sent a dispatch, and I said that: "On the basis of the conclusions reached at the meeting in Banja Luka on the 11th of February, 1992, please set up and have a meeting with all senior officials of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in your area and report to me accordingly." That is to say, it was not a secret meeting. After that, I gave this order, or, rather, I asked that all senior personnel be informed about this of all ethnic backgrounds, Serbs, Croats and Muslims, in order to place relations on a sound basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's precisely what I want to do ask you about. It doesn't say here that Serb representatives should be informed; rather, what it says here is that all senior-level personnel should be informed?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, we just wanted to work in a lawful manner and to observe regulations that were in force, nothing more than that. There was no reason for us to inform some and not others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we know whether this telegram was sent along regular channels in police communications or were some secret channels reported to?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you see number 02 up here? That is my department. That is the number of my department. And there is the number of the dispatch; that is to say, it is being centre to the Centre of Communications, and the employees who are there are sending it further on to the addressees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since this has already been admitted -- so this was archived; right? It was probably from the archives, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all the mentioned centres received this, and of course it was in MUP headquarters as well, because 02 was my department, and the Police Administration was 01, and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now have 1D1899.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, in English, there is this phrase "kick him up," and I'll tell you what that means. Was this appointment of Mico Stanisic something like that? How do you see it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this meeting, the reaction was that Mico Stanisic, who was until then the chief of the Sarajevo police, of the SUP of Sarajevo, not the Sarajevo Centre, he was supposed to be appointed adviser in the Office of the Minister of the Interior, an adviser for state security affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we scroll up a bit? What did that mean? Was this a proper promotion or was this done in order to remove him from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until then, Mico Stanisic was in the town of Sarajevo, itself. He was invited to the minister's office to be an adviser to the minister, or, rather, to Brano Kvesic. Of course, advisers are people who are not in charge of operations, who do not have resources. They have nothing. Instead of him, Kemal Sabovic was appointed. I think he was an ethnic Muslim, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this was a position that belonged to the Serbs. So a Serb was ostensibly promoted to a higher post, but instead of him, a non-Serb was appointed to the original position?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters. This is probably way too fast. Can this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Kemal Sabovic, is that the Muslim in question?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think we have a hard copy -- this appears to be a duplicate of 17184. I'm checking it against the screen, and most of what I see appears to match.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we confirm with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And here's a hard copy of the document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you put it on the ELMO? Yes, I think the number matches. The date is also consistent. Yes, we'll admit this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D382, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 1896, please. Could we have that in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, do you recall that in the previous document, one of the Serbs mentioned that thousands of Motorolas were purchased and that not a single one of them entered MUP warehouses and storage facilities, or, rather, was not recorded at all?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we are going to see what happened on the 27th of February, 1992. Kemal Sabovic or Kemal Sabovic, who you mentioned, who replaced Mico Stanisic -- did with a number of those Motorolas. Can you read that and explain it to us?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Official Note, compiled at the Ministry of the Interior of the SR BH, in connection with taking over hand-held radio sets, Motorola MX-330." "On the 27th of February, 1991, in the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the presence of Kemal Sabovic, chief of the MUP police, hand-held Motorola radios were handed over, MX-330, to a representative of the Party of Democratic Action, Selver Mahmutovic," and then his ID number and so on and so forth. And then the actual numbers are referred to; that is to say, which hand-held radios, and which type, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that Motorolas are well known, but would you tell the participants in these proceedings what a Motorola is and what this is all about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are wireless hand-held radios that are used by the police and the military for communication, for wireless communication on special channels.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D383, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 18927, please. Could we have that now, and we're probably going to need the assistance of the OTP in this respect, or the witness, too, yes, certainly, the witness. The witness will certainly be in a position to tell us what he knows. 18267 is the 65 ter number. No, it's not this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see here that this is some information that is a state secret, strictly confidential? Can you read this out?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "State Secret, strictly confidential, filed in three copies. "Information on abuse, illegal action, and manipulation by personnel of the SDA and the HDZ in the State Security Service of the MUP of the SR BH, through personnel policy, new organisation and staffing systems, and the one-sided application of methods, and resources in the work of the service in the interests of the coalition Yoke between the SDA and the HDZ, to the detriment of the Serb people, and the policy of the SDS, and a proposal as to how to overcome these problems."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the bottom of the page? Can we see the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "March 1992."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is there a translation of this document, by any chance? Can we establish that? No. All right. Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, you are familiar with the phenomena referred to in this information, and you have talked to us about them already. Do you know about the document, itself?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I should just like us to read some things which are of the essence. For instance, the SDB is the secret police, in current conditions it should have to be equally in the service of the parties in power. However, this service has so far been only serving the SDA and the HDZ for the following reasons: "From the time of the multi-party elections to date, the personnel policy in the State Security Service of the MUP of the SR BH, on behalf of the SDS, has been conducted and is being conducted by Hilmo Selimovic, Asim Dautbasic, Munir Alibabic, and Branko Kvesic." Am I right when I say this is the self-same Munir or Munja Alibabic who was prohibited from working in the police for life?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the proposal of Ms. Carla Del Ponte, this was issued, this prohibition, by the representative of the OHR in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is any of these people a Serb?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now they describe here all the things which had been done. The SDS was given the 5th and 6th Administrations and one department which objectively were of peripheral importance in relation to the other operational administrations. Then, in the next paragraph, a bit down: "The disobedient Serbs -- scores should be settled with disobedient Serbs (disobedient without choosing the means), Radomir Ninkovic, Dusan Neskovic, Nedjo Vlaski, Zoran Renovica, Tomo Puhalac, and others." What happened to these people? How were scores settled with them?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were dismissed from work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When drawing up a new organisational layout and staffing scheme of the SDB in March 1991, as Asim Dautbasic, Munir Alibabic, and Branko Kvesic, instead of the office of deputy under secretary for the State Security Service, which according to the inter-party agreement was due to the SDS (pushed through to less-important assistance posts). In this way, the SDS lost man number two in the SDB service. The first one was to be held by a Croat, which was to organise, plan, and co-ordinate all activities of the operational complement of the service." Can I jog your memory or check this: When these officers were being signed, we were told the minister should be a Muslim, but all the operational officers should be -- should go to the others, to the Serbs, and was this the way it was supposed to have been?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here we see that this operational office, in charge of the operational segment, was to have been through the position of the deputy?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as the operational activities are concerned in SDB, the post of assistant of deputy is much more important than any other place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And they abolished specifically that position so that no Serb would be in that important position?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Major Vlaski, to the best of my recollection, was to have been that person. But he never worked anywhere, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we have an entire list of instances of abuses from March 1991; namely, two months after the election of the coalition government, machinations had already begun whereby the Serb people were dis-enfranchised, and their power that was due to them was taken away from them in this way; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the State Security Service is concerned, never were all the senior posts filled in that service.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move on to page 3, the third page of this document. It is 7760, the number on the top. This is what it says: "In such a constellation of relations in the State Security Service in the past period, emphasis in the work of the service was placed almost exclusively on operational research and the documenting of activities within the SDS."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Meaning that the entire -- the concern of the SDB was to monitor the activities of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To monitor the activities of one of the parties in power, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And towards the bottom, they say: "From May 1992, the telephone was wire-tapped in the SDS Deputy's Club which was often used by Radovan Karadzic, who they monitored under the pseudonym 'Doctor,' and Vojislav Maksimovic, whose house number was also placed under surveillance." Do you remember that Vojislav Maksimovic initially was a non-party person and the president of the Serbian MPs' caucus, of the Serbian Deputy Club in the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojislav Maksimovic is a university professor, and he was the president of the Deputy's Club in the joint Parliament. You liked these professors, President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is an objection in keeping with what Bismark had said; 12 professors and the fatherland is lost. Bismark did not like them all that much. Mr. Minister, what was necessary for the telephone of the Deputy's Club and the private telephone of the president of the Deputy's Club to be wire-tapped, whether that party be in the opposition or in power?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what is required for approval to wire-tap the telephone of an ordinary citizen. What was required was a decision by the competent judge of the District Court in the area, and he should have committed some crime against -- one of the more serious crimes against the state. At that time, we did not have crimes of terrorism and crimes of the kind that are now happening in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but there were crimes against the state system, against the people and country, et cetera. That was as far as ordinary citizens were concerned. But to listen in on the telephone of an MP or an official in the government, I don't even know there was legal provision for that at all. There was no legal possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would it have been necessary for his immunity to have been waived, lifted, in Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is another thing. If there was a pre-trial procedure and then a criminal procedure instituted against such a person, and the prosecutor placed such a request before the judge in question, then the Parliament would lift the immunity of the MP in question, or of another official, which I actually tried to explain to Their Honours yesterday. Namely, in the case of the president of the Ilidza municipality, we had a similar situation, and only then can such measures be applied.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see the next page. Let's see. Here we have the names of all the people they wire-tapped; Koljevic, Krajisnik, Milorad Ekmecic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Milorad Ekmecic is one of the most imminent, one of the most prominent historians of the former Yugoslavia and a member of the Academy of Sciences of Yugoslavia and Academy of Arts and Sciences of Bosnia-Herzegovina and of many academies in the world?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the most imminent historians, not only in the former Yugoslavia, but I believe also in the whole of Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So they listen in to Mico Stanisic, the president of the Ilijas municipality, the chief of the Nova Sarajevo Public Security Station, and they say: "In addition to the existing listening points, they also set up a new one at Zlatiste --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's on the way to Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- where only Muslim activists of the SDA work, Behmen Arnautovic, Skalonja, and others. All the material from these check-points and written materials are directly brought to Munir Alibabic and, through Dautbasic, Kvesic, Hebib and Delimustafic, are directly submitted to the leaders of the SDA and the HDZ." Was that so?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say -- to describe what the illegal activities of the SDA in 1991. The service came by verified data on the illegal imports of weapons for the SDA through the Libyan Consulate, and this job directly involved, on behalf of the SDA, Naim Kadic, a colleague of mine, by the way, Rusmir Mahmutcehajic, and Alija Delimustafic, and they go on to refer to the countries through which the arms were imported; Austria, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, et cetera. Let us not dwell on this at length, but let us look at the following two pages, so the next one and the fifth page of this document. Is this, what I have just read, consistent with what you know?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is consistent with what I know and it is consistent with the truth, because we do have all these conversations of Munir Alibabic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "In order to overcome the problems and strike a balance in the service of the MUP of the BH regarding the SDA and the HDZ, we propose the following:" And then they have a list of measures: "Immediately take measures to replace inadequate Serbian personnel in the MUP." Then the personnel have to be professional, not discredited, and uncompromisingly ready to fight for the Serbian people, but within the constitutional and legal regulations.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have the text on their screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They also are asking for immediate appointment of deputy chief in the Sarajevo Sector, which office initially was agreed to belong to the SDS, according to the inter-party agreement. Mr. Minister, did these proposals and the people who proposed them instill hope that there would be no war in March?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For had they known that there would be war, would they be proposing these measures?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, you said you knew this document. Tell us -- if you could tell us what document it is about. Whose document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is a report of certain officials of Serb ethnicity of the State Security Service; a report by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. That will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D384, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I forgot to ask you, Mr. Mandic, whether you saw this document at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
