utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot recall when it was that I saw it first, but I was familiar with it. I'm certain of that, because I was in charge of all the personnel. I was the focal point of all developments in the police then. Namely, I cannot remember the specific time, but I certainly knew before the war of these positions and these conclusions, and the attempts to appoint in the State Security Service Serbian personnel, but that did not happen in -- did not happen for a whole year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we have 10 more minutes for today, but the Chamber has allowed you 20 minutes for your cross-examination for this witness, Mr. Mandic. I'm sorry, 20 hours, I should have said, 20 hours. Not 20 minutes, of course. And you have spent so far a bit more than six hours, almost one-third of it, albeit under the control of the Chamber. It is for you how to use those 20 hours, but speaking for myself, I'm of the impression that you are concentrating somewhat on narrow issues. So I would like you to move on to more relevant issues tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Excellency, to me, as a Freudian psychologist, this Freudian slip of yours tells me that you are quite conscious of the fact that 20 hours is not enough for me, and I do hope that you will treat me generously in that respect. As regards the presentation -- as regards the presentation, I should like to say this: If I have been indicted of a joint criminal enterprise, I do agree that there was a joint criminal enterprise, but not on the Serbian side. We have to show what it was that we had been confronted with, what the challenges were, what the threat was to the survival of Serbs, and we shall prove that what had been envisaged was that there should be no Serbs in Bosnia, and you will see that. How else could I do that but through a man who was not an SDS member, but who was a professional, who was a judge, who was a policeman, who was in the very center of developments? We have to put together this picture. What had led to the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, who wanted that war, and what the conditions were. I know that you want me to paint this in wider strokes, but here we have a person who, himself, with a heavy heart, wrote certain documents, addressing very relevant addressees in Bosnia and Herzegovina, to tell them that Bosnia was heading for disaster. That is why I believe that we should look at all these documents and put together this picture from the smaller tiles in the mosaic. All this actually led to the creation of an unlawful army in the Croat-Muslim section of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's not waste time anymore, but please bear that in mind, the Chamber will consider how efficiently you have spent your time when there is a request for you for additional time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: And, Dr. Karadzic, as a Freudian, you'll no doubt recall when considering the issue of relevancy, that the first serious academic paper that Dr. Sigmund Freud ever wrote was about the gonads of eels.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are quite right, but we'll go on. Can we have 1D1210. These are minutes from the session which we referred to previously of the 2nd of March, 1992. I believe that we had played a magnetophone, a tape-recorder recording, but these are minutes which are a bit more succinct, not verbatim, but just reflect the essence of the conclusions reached at that session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to read not the heading, but the -- what is this about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only have the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, minutes.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Minutes of the 56th Session of the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, held on the 2nd of March, 1992. "Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina," number and date: "The session was held in two parts. The first part of the session began at 11.00 a.m. and ended at 12.00."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the second part?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second part of the session began at 1830 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see from here that Alija Izetbegovic was present, who was in the chair, and also Biljana Plavsic, Franjo Boras, and Ejub Ganic, the secretaries, the prime minister, the deputy prime ministers, namely, the prime minister, Jure Pelivan, and Muhamed Cengic, Alija Delimustafic, and Vitomir Zepinic, his deputy, and commander of the Military District Kukanjac, and the commander of the Republican Territorial Defence Staff? Can we go to page 2 in the Serbian? And in English, we still have it on the screen. So in the second part, after their meeting: "In the second part, also participated the president of the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Democratic Party [indiscernible] Rajko Dukic ..." Do you remember, Mr. Minister, that all of Croatia had a crisis staff in every single municipality from the very beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina or Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Croatia, Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the SDA started to set up its crisis staffs throughout Bosnia? Towards the end of March and the beginning of April; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we have been there. We have gone through that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that the Presidency, I believe, set up its Crisis Staff on the 20th of September, and Biljana Plavsic was against it and later Nikola Koljevic, who was not at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see -- do we see that this meeting was organised in connection with this agenda? Can we see English page 2, the next one. And Fikret Abdic, Nikola Koljevic and Stjepan Kljujic are absent, and the agenda was to consider the situation following the blockade of Sarajevo traffic routes, as well as the general situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was because of the murder of a wedding party member in 1992 in Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here, we see in bold face, the Presidency stating: "Namely, in addition to that situation --" Aha, no, item 1: "The president has condemned the tragic incident which happened on the 29th of February this year in the old part of Sarajevo, as well as any other act of violence." And it demands that measures be taken and that the perpetrators be brought to justice. In the beginning of your testimony, you told us that you knew where this perpetrator -- where this killer of the wedding party guest was, but there was no way you could get to him and arrest him?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This hapless event which happened near the old church, which was built in 1200 and something and is one of the oldest edifices or places of worship in Sarajevo, this the father of the bridegroom was killed because he was brandishing a Serbian flag. The wedding party was proceeding on foot towards the church. As is Christian, or, rather, Orthodox custom, wedding parties, when they go to church, are unarmed. They cannot -- may not carry arms. Asim Delalic killed a man just for carrying a Serbian flag in Bascarsija. Immediately, we found out who the perpetrator and who the co-perpetrator was, but --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's it for today, because there's another trial, so we have to conclude here today. I note this document has been admitted as Exhibit D214, being marked for identification, the reason being because there was no full translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's clearly excerpted portions, and that, I think, was the source of the concern and issue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I say this is not a transcript. These are minutes. I'm not sure what was offered, the transcript or the minutes, but I should like it to be translated in total because it is very instructive, because at this meeting the Presidency accepted its own mistakes and concluded that they should be rectified. On the basis of these minutes, I sent a document for appointments to be made in the police. In other words, they are connected. I should like to ask that the entire document be translated, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It was put to Mr. Colm Doyle, who couldn't confirm the content of it. But having heard the evidence who confirmed the content of it, we'll still keep the status pending translation. We'll resume again tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 8th day of July, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
